title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #5

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sound is whispered, with no buzz in the throat? (1 mark)
   A. /g/
   B. /v/
   C. /f/
   D. /d/

2. Which of these is a reference material? (1 mark)
   A. A letter
   B. A dictionary
   C. A song
   D. A storybook

3. If the guide words are 'farm' and 'feast', which word is on that page? (1 mark)
   A. apple
   B. fashion
   C. zebra
   D. mango

4. Which word is a definite article? (1 mark)
   A. a
   B. an
   C. the
   D. some

5. Which is safe when filling an online form? (1 mark)
   A. Give your password to any site
   B. Fill it in secret
   C. Fill it with a parent or teacher
   D. Share your address with strangers

6. Which word means 'to make a place pretty with balloons and ribbons'? (1 mark)
   A. attend
   B. graduate
   C. celebrate
   D. decorate

7. What does the saying 'Unity is strength' mean? (1 mark)
   A. The strongest person always wins
   B. Nobody needs friends
   C. People are stronger when they work together
   D. Only leaders are strong

8. Which plural is irregular? (1 mark)
   A. dishes
   B. boxes
   C. books
   D. children

9. What is the first step in writing a composition? (1 mark)
   A. Plan your ideas
   B. Write the conclusion
   C. Copy a story
   D. Draw a picture only

10. What is a good way to find the meaning of an unknown word in a passage? (1 mark)
   A. Guess without reading
   B. Read the sentences around it for clues
   C. Skip the passage
   D. Ask a stranger

11. Which word contains the blend 'tr'? (1 mark)
   A. snake
   B. flag
   C. clap
   D. train

12. Which letter is silent in 'write'? (1 mark)
   A. i
   B. r
   C. w
   D. t

13. The verb 'record' (to make a record) is stressed on (1 mark)
   A. neither
   B. the second syllable
   C. both
   D. the first syllable

14. If you face the rising sun, north is on your (1 mark)
   A. back
   B. left
   C. right
   D. front

15. Which is a minimal pair for /f/ and /v/? (1 mark)
   A. book, look
   B. jam, ham
   C. pen, pin
   D. safe, save

16. The short form of 'I would' is (1 mark)
   A. I'd
   B. I've
   C. I'm
   D. I'll

17. Which phrase has adjectives in the correct order? (1 mark)
   A. a round small red ball
   B. a round red small ball
   C. a small round red ball
   D. a red round small ball

18. Which word is the opposite of plump? (1 mark)
   A. round
   B. big
   C. healthy
   D. thin

19. What is a password? (1 mark)
   A. A secret word that only you know
   B. A friend's address
   C. A type of email
   D. A public name

20. Which is a polite offer? (1 mark)
   A. Would you like some tea?
   B. Would you like many tea?
   C. You would like a lot tea?
   D. Would you like much tea bags?

21. In a picture series, which picture usually shows the ending? (1 mark)
   A. The last picture
   B. The first picture
   C. The middle picture
   D. None of them

22. Which is a good listening habit? (1 mark)
   A. Talk to your neighbour
   B. Look out of the window
   C. Look at the speaker
   D. Shout answers before the question ends

23. What is extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Studying one text word by word with the teacher
   B. Reading only for a test
   C. Copying notes from the board
   D. Choosing materials and reading a lot on your own for pleasure and learning

24. How do you make the question form of 'She is reading'? (1 mark)
   A. Is she reading?
   B. Is reading she?
   C. Does she reading?
   D. She is reading?

25. Which sentence is a run-on sentence that needs full stops? (1 mark)
   A. I bought fish.
   B. I went to the market I bought fish we went home.
   C. I went to the market.
   D. We went home.

26. What is fertilizer used for? (1 mark)
   A. To store water
   B. To dig the soil
   C. To kill birds
   D. To help plants grow

27. Which pair of words differs only because of /v/ and /w/? (1 mark)
   A. bell and bill
   B. vet and wet
   C. sip and chip
   D. sit and sat

28. 'It's' is a short form of which words? (1 mark)
   A. it was only
   B. it is or it has
   C. it will only
   D. its own

29. Which simile compares using 'as ... as'? (1 mark)
   A. The tall maize stood.
   B. The maize like a door.
   C. The maize was as tall as a door.
   D. The maize grew tall.

30. What should you do if you find a needle or razor blade on the ground? (1 mark)
   A. Play with it
   B. Pick it up and keep it
   C. Give it to a younger child
   D. Not touch it and tell a trusted adult

31. What does a dictionary give? (1 mark)
   A. News about sports
   B. A map of Kenya
   C. A list of names of people
   D. The meaning and spelling of words

32. Why do flies spread germs? (1 mark)
   A. They land on waste and then on food
   B. They sleep on beds
   C. They eat all the soap
   D. They drink clean water

33. What does 'for' mean when it is used as a conjunction? (1 mark)
   A. before
   B. however
   C. although
   D. because

34. Which sentence uses the sense of touch? (1 mark)
   A. The soup tasted sweet.
   B. The towel is soft and dry.
   C. We heard laughter.
   D. The room is bright.

35. What does a referee do? (1 mark)
   A. Sells tickets
   B. Controls a game and makes sure the rules are followed
   C. Trains the team
   D. Cleans the field

36. Which word begins with the voiced sound /ð/? (1 mark)
   A. thumb
   B. think
   C. three
   D. this

37. In the passage about netball, how many players are in a team? (1 mark)
   A. nine
   B. eleven
   C. seven
   D. five

38. Which word begins with the cluster 'br'? (1 mark)
   A. clap
   B. sweep
   C. grass
   D. broom

39. Which syllable is stressed in 'com-POUND'? (1 mark)
   A. Neither
   B. The second
   C. The first
   D. Both equally

40. Which sentence uses the past perfect? (1 mark)
   A. I had finished before he came.
   B. I finish.
   C. I have finished.
   D. I am finishing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. List the three parts of a narrative and say what each tells. (3 marks)

42. Make a simple plan for a story called 'The Guests Who Came Late'. (4 marks)

43. Describe how to make the sounds /f/ and /v/ and say how they are different. Give one example pair. (4 marks)

44. List three parts of a diary entry. (3 marks)

45. Explain the difference between 'but' and 'so' with an example of each. (4 marks)

46. Use the words 'sibling', 'relative' and 'chore' in three sentences about a family. (3 marks)

47. State two habits of a good listener. (2 marks)

48. Give two nonverbal cues that show a speaker is confident. (2 marks)

49. Explain how guide words help you find a word quickly. (3 marks)

50. Fill in the double letters: di__er, ye__ow, bu__on. (3 marks)

51. Give three words with silent letters and name the silent letter in each. (3 marks)

52. Write four sentences about cleaning your classroom that use and, but, so and or. (4 marks)

53. Cross out the silent letter in each word: write, lamb, honest, listen. (2 marks)

54. What is a nonverbal cue? Give two examples. (3 marks)

55. Write two words in which 'gh' is silent and two in which it says /f/. (4 marks)

56. Correct this sentence and explain: 'I don't have no seeds.' (3 marks)

57. Explain how intonation can change the meaning of 'Really?' (3 marks)

58. Correct the paragraph: 'last friday our class visited the museum. mr. juma told us about kenya.' (4 marks)

59. Correct these sentences: (a) Who did scored the goal? (b) When you will come? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — /f/
   /f/ is a whispered sound. /v/, /d/ and /g/ are voiced.

2. B — A dictionary
   A dictionary is used to look up spelling and meaning, so it is a reference book.

3. B — fashion
   Fashion comes after farm and before feast in the alphabet.

4. C — the
   The is the definite article.

5. C — Fill it with a parent or teacher
   A trusted adult can help you keep your details safe.

6. D — decorate
   To decorate is to make a place look pretty.

7. C — People are stronger when they work together
   Working together makes a group stronger.

8. D — children
   Child becomes children, not childs.

9. A — Plan your ideas
   A plan puts ideas in order first.

10. B — Read the sentences around it for clues
   Context clues help you understand new words.

11. D — train
   Train begins with t and r.

12. C — w
   We say rite, so the w is silent.

13. B — the second syllable
   The verb is re-CORD.

14. B — left
   The sun rises in the east. When you face east, north is on your left.

15. D — safe, save
   They differ in the last sound.

16. A — I'd
   I would can be shortened to I'd.

17. C — a small round red ball
   The order is size, shape, colour.

18. D — thin
   Plump means fat in a pleasant way and thin is its opposite.

19. A — A secret word that only you know
   A password protects your account.

20. A — Would you like some tea?
   We use some in offers.

21. A — The last picture
   The last picture usually shows how it finished.

22. C — Look at the speaker
   Looking at the speaker shows you are listening.

23. D — Choosing materials and reading a lot on your own for pleasure and learning
   Extensive reading is wide, independent reading.

24. A — Is she reading?
   Put is before the subject.

25. B — I went to the market I bought fish we went home.
   Three ideas are run together without full stops.

26. D — To help plants grow
   Fertilizer adds nutrients to soil.

27. B — vet and wet
   In 'vet' and 'wet' only the first sound differs.

28. B — it is or it has
   It's = it is / it has.

29. C — The maize was as tall as a door.
   'As tall as a door' is an as ... as simile.

30. D — Not touch it and tell a trusted adult
   Sharp objects may carry germs.

31. D — The meaning and spelling of words
   Dictionary words are in alphabetical order.

32. A — They land on waste and then on food
   Flies carry germs from waste to food.

33. D — because
   'For' gives a reason.

34. B — The towel is soft and dry.
   'Soft and dry' describes how it feels.

35. B — Controls a game and makes sure the rules are followed
   A referee is the official in charge.

36. D — this
   'This' has the voiced 'th'.

37. C — seven
   The passage says two teams of seven players.

38. D — broom
   'Broom' begins with b and r.

39. B — The second
   The stress falls on 'pound'.

40. A — I had finished before he came.
   Had + past participle.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: who, where and when. Middle: the events. End: how it finished.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: family prepares for a party. Middle: guests do not arrive, food gets cold. Problem: they lost the way. End: they arrive, everyone laughs and eats.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a beginning, 1 for events, 1 for a problem and 1 for an ending.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Touch the top teeth to the lower lip and blow. /f/ is whispered and /v/ is voiced with a buzz. Example: fan and van.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mouth position, 1 mark for /f/ whispered, 1 mark for /v/ voiced, 1 mark for the pair.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Day and date; greeting (Dear Diary); body (events and feelings); sign-off. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: 'But' shows a difference: It was late, but we stayed. 'So' shows a result: It was late, so we left.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: My sibling is my little sister. My aunt is a relative. My chore is to sweep the yard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker and keep quiet until the speaker has finished a whole idea. Nodding to show you follow is also correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct habit.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Eye contact and standing straight; a smile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Guide words show the first and last word on a page. If your word comes between them alphabetically, it is on that page. If not, turn forward or backward.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what guide words show, 1 mark for comparing your word, 1 mark for turning pages.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: dinner, yellow, button
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: knee (k), debt (b), honest (h).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word with its silent letter.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four correct sentences, each with the named conjunction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: write (w), lamb (b), honest (h), listen (t)
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: A nonverbal cue is a message sent without words. Examples: a smile shows happiness; a thumbs-up shows approval.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 for each example.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Silent: night, light, high, daughter (any two). /f/: laugh, cough, enough, rough (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: I don't have any seeds (or: I have no seeds). English uses only one negative word here.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct sentence, 2 marks for the explanation.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: A high rising voice shows surprise, while a low falling voice shows the speaker is not interested. So the tune of the voice shows feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way and 1 mark for linking to feelings.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Last Friday our class visited the museum. Mr. Juma told us about Kenya.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for Last Friday, Mr. Juma, Kenya and correct full stops.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) Who scored the goal? (b) When will you come?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correction and 1 for question marks and capitals.
